_doc: Maps each [VISUAL: image src=...] / [VISUAL: diagram src=...] semantic id from script.md to a file under videos/galois-life-and-contributions-3/. Some semantic ids point to the same physical file when the visual context is the same (e.g. all manuscript-* cues use the actual Galois letter to Chevalier; the recurring 'galois-sketch-portrait' is one file referenced 6 times).

galois-sketch-portrait.caption: Posthumous portrait of Évariste Galois drawn from memory by his brother Alfred Galois, c.1848.

manuscript-page-marginalia.caption: An example of one of Galois's extant drafts (some are much clearer).

paris-pond-dawn-corot.caption: 'Pond at Ville-d'Avray' by Camille Corot, late 1860s — used as visual stand-in for the dawn pond near the Faultrier pension.

manuscript-je-nai-pas-le-temps.caption: Final page of Galois's mathematical testament (letter to Auguste Chevalier, 29 May 1832), in his own hand. Contains the phrase often paraphrased as 'Je n'ai pas le temps'.

bourg-la-reine-engraving.caption: Bourg-la-Reine, l'Église et la Mairie. Antique postcard of Galois's birth-town town centre.
bourg-la-reine-engraving.attribution: Postcard, Archives départementales des Hauts-de-Seine, public domain

napoleon-hundred-days.caption: Joseph Beaume, 'Napoléon Ier quittant l'île d'Elbe' (1836). Visual stand-in for the Hundred Days of 1815.

restoration-france-engraving.caption: François Joseph Heim, 'Charles X distributing awards to artists at the 1824 Salon, January 15, 1825' (1827). Iconic image of the Bourbon Restoration.

paris-1823-louis-le-grand-engraving.caption: Cour d'honneur du Lycée Louis-le-Grand. Used at beat-015 as Galois enters the school in 1823.

louis-le-grand-classroom.method: hand-coded SVG, 1920x1080, period-style classroom with arched windows, blackboard reading 'x² − 5x + 6 = 0', silhouetted students. Caption: Vernier's first mathematics class, February 1827.

legendre-geometry-page.method: hand-coded SVG mock title page of Legendre's 'Élémens de Géométrie' (1794 ed), with period typography, ornament rules and a small geometric figure. Used because no clean Wikimedia scan exists.

ruffini-portrait.caption: Paolo Ruffini (1765–1822). Portrait by Biagio Magnanini (Modena). Italian mathematician who in 1799 attempted a proof that the quintic is unsolvable by radicals.

abel-portrait.caption: Niels Henrik Abel (1802–1829), lithograph after a drawing by Johan Gørbitz.
abel-portrait.attribution: Trondheim Municipal Archives, via Wikimedia Commons

academy-of-sciences-paris.caption: L'Académie des Sciences et des Beaux Arts, Paris. 19th-century engraving.

cauchy-portrait.caption: Augustin-Louis Cauchy (1789–1857), lithograph by Rudolph Hoffmann after a photograph by Bertsch, 1856.
cauchy-portrait.attribution: Smithsonian Libraries Dibner Collection, via Wikimedia Commons

taton-letter-1971.caption: René Taton (1915–2004), the historian of science whose 1971 archival find rehabilitated Cauchy's reputation regarding Galois's manuscript.
taton-letter-1971.attribution: International Academy of the History of Science (Académie Internationale d'Histoire des Sciences), via Wikimedia Commons

paris-rue-jean-de-beauvais.caption: Charles Marville, 'Rue Jean-de-Beauvais', Paris (c.1865). The street where Nicolas-Gabriel Galois ended his life, two steps from Louis-le-Grand.

bourg-la-reine-funeral.method: hand-coded SVG. Period-style cortège silhouette: small church, dark figures bearing a coffin, faint stones being thrown, Bourg-la-Reine caption. No specific Wikimedia image of Nicolas-Gabriel Galois's funeral exists.

ecole-polytechnique-engraving.caption: École polytechnique — façade. Period photograph from BnF Gallica.

ecole-normale-superieure.caption: École Normale, Rue d'Ulm — dessin par H. Clerget. 19th-century architectural drawing.
ecole-normale-superieure.attribution: H. Clerget, BnF Gallica, public domain

fourier-portrait.caption: Joseph Fourier (1768–1830). Galois's 1830 Grand Prize entry was sent to him; Fourier died in April, manuscript lost.

liberty-leading-the-people-delacroix.caption: Eugène Delacroix, 'La Liberté guidant le peuple' (1830). Commemorates the July Revolution / Trois Glorieuses.
liberty-leading-the-people-delacroix.attribution: Eugène Delacroix (1798–1863), Musée du Louvre, public domain

gazette-des-ecoles.caption: Galois's first published article (1829) — used as period-stand-in for the 1830 Gazette des Écoles open letter.

artillery-national-guard-uniform.method: hand-coded SVG. Stylized Artillerie de la Garde Nationale uniform, c.1830: bicorne with red plume, navy coat with red lapels, white sash, crossed-cannon insignia, sabre. With annotation lines.

vendanges-bourgogne-banquet.method: hand-coded SVG. Long banquet table under a hanging lamp: silhouettes of guests, Galois standing centre with knife and glass, Dumas leaping toward window. Caption: Vendanges des Bourgogne, May 9 1831.

alexandre-dumas-portrait.caption: Alexandre Dumas père, photograph by Félix Nadar, 1855.
alexandre-dumas-portrait.attribution: Nadar, Google Art Project, public domain

paris-1831-arrest.method: hand-coded SVG. Night scene: building façade with two lit windows, lamp post, two dark agent figures escorting a smaller silhouette. Caption: Paris, May 10, 1831.

bastille-day-1831.method: hand-coded SVG. July Column silhouette with Génie statue, lone figure in National Guard Artillery uniform with rifle/pistols/dagger. Caption: Bastille Day, July 14, 1831.

sainte-pelagie-prison.caption: La prison de Sainte-Pélagie — Le Greffe (the registry).

raspail-portrait.caption: François-Vincent Raspail (1794–1878), republican prisoner who kept letters from Sainte-Pélagie.

poisson-portrait.caption: E. Marcellot, Portrait of Siméon-Denis Poisson, 1804.

manuscript-preface.caption: Reuse of the Galois letter image as visual stand-in for the December 1831 Préface (no separate facsimile of the Préface page is on Wikimedia).

paris-1832-cholera.caption: Alfred Rethel, 'Der Tod als Würger' / 'Death the Strangler — Cholera's First Appearance at a Masked Ball in Paris 1831'. Iconic period print of the 1832 cholera epidemic.

manuscript-erased-name.caption: The Galois letter — used here as stand-in for the manuscripts on which Infantozzi (1968) read Stéphanie's name beneath erasures.

stephanie-letters-on-back-of-math-paper.caption: Galois's mathematical manuscript page (last letter) — visual stand-in for the math manuscript onto which Galois copied Stéphanie's letters.

manuscript-letter-to-chevalier.caption: Final page of Évariste Galois's letter to Auguste Chevalier, written 29 May 1832, containing the bulk of his mathematical testament.

je-nai-pas-le-temps-marginalia.caption: Galois's letter — the famous 'Je n'ai pas le temps' margin annotation appears once on this manuscript. Cue uses zoom=true to crop in on the marginalia.

pescheux-dherbinville.method: hand-coded SVG. Empty oval portrait frame in 19th-century style with anonymous silhouette and faint question mark — no portrait of Pescheux d'Herbinville survives.

hospital-cochin-19th-century.caption: Historic entrance of Hôpital Cochin, Paris (where Galois died on June 1, 1832).

paris-funeral-1832.method: hand-coded SVG. Vast crowd silhouette under twilight sky with Notre-Dame skyline, two layers of mourners. Caption: June 2, 1832, Montparnasse.

manuscript-stack-on-desk.caption: 1830 contract — visual stand-in for the bundle of Galois manuscripts left to Alfred and Chevalier.

journal-de-liouville-1846.caption: Title page of the Journal de Mathématiques pures et appliquées (Journal de Liouville). Galois's memoir was published here in 1846.

jordan-traite-1870.method: hand-coded SVG mock title page of Camille Jordan's 'Traité des substitutions et des équations algébriques' (Paris: Gauthier-Villars, MDCCCLXX). Includes a centred composition-series ornament G > H > K > ⋯ > {e}.

erlangen-programme.caption: Felix Klein (1849–1925), the father of the Erlangen Programme (1872).

conservation-laws-symmetries.method: hand-coded SVG. Three columns: time-translation→energy, space-translation→momentum, U(1) phase rotation→charge. Visualizes Noether's 1918 theorem.

standard-model-lagrangian.method: hand-coded SVG. SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) tile row plus expanded Standard Model Lagrangian beneath, with each gauge term colour-tagged to its group.

qr-code-and-cd.method: hand-coded SVG. QR code on the left, rainbow CD on the right, central GF(2⁸) box. Reed–Solomon caption.

rsa-key-visualization.method: hand-coded SVG. Gold padlock, two columns of streaming hex digits (cipher streams), modular-exponentiation formula c = m^e mod N, caption about (ℤ/Nℤ)*.

wiles-fermat-portrait.caption: Andrew Wiles, Boston 1995. Photo by Klaus Barner.
